prompt_inputs.mapping_sheet: CUST_ID (source: NUMBER(10), target: INTEGER, required: Y, rule: Direct mapping) | CUST_NAME (source: VARCHAR2(100), target: VARCHAR(100), required: Y, rule: TRIM and UPPER) | EMAIL (source: VARCHAR2(50), target: VARCHAR(50), required: N, rule: Validate format, reject if invalid) | CUST_STATUS (source: CHAR(1), target: CHAR(1), required: Y, rule: Map A→Active, I→Inactive) | LAST_UPDATED (source: DATE, target: TIMESTAMP, required: Y, rule: Convert to UTC) | PHONE (source: VARCHAR2(20), target: VARCHAR(20), required: N, rule: Remove non-numeric except +/-) | ADDRESS (source: VARCHAR2(200), target: VARCHAR(200), required: N, rule: Standardize format)
prompt_inputs.overview_sheet: Workflow: [Extract from Oracle] → [Data Quality Validation] → [Transform & Cleanse] → [Duplicate Detection] → [Error Handling & Logging] → [Retry Mechanism (max 3 attempts)] → [Load to PostgreSQL] → [Reconciliation Report]. Extract Phase: Query CUST_MASTER with incremental load (delta detection via LAST_UPDATED). Validation Phase: Check NOT NULL constraints, data type compliance, email format validation. Transform Phase: Apply mapping rules, standardize formats, handle NULL values. Duplicate Detection: Compare CUST_ID and EMAIL against existing records, flag duplicates. Error Handling: Log failed records with error codes, route to quarantine table. Retry: Implement exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) for transient failures. Load Phase: Batch insert with transaction rollback on critical errors. Reconciliation: Compare record counts and checksums between source and target.

prompt_inputs.sheet:
Base Design Document - Real-time Streaming ETL Migration

History Updated: 2024-01-15
Current State: Batch processing runs nightly with 8-hour latency
Target State: Real-time streaming with <5 minute latency requirement

Sender Spec:
- Source: Oracle OLTP Database (Orders, Customers, Transactions tables)
- Current: Daily batch export at 2 AM UTC
- Target: Kafka topic with event streaming
- Volume: 50K transactions/hour average, 200K peak

Receiver Spec:
- Target: Snowflake Data Warehouse
- Current: Nightly load via SFTP
- Target: Continuous ingestion via Snowflake Kafka connector
- SLA: 95th percentile latency <5 minutes

Mapping:
- Orders table → orders_stream topic → fct_orders table
- Customers table → customers_stream topic → dim_customers table
- Transactions table → transactions_stream topic → fct_transactions table
prompt_inputs.mapping_sheet:
| Physical Column | Logical Column | Data Type | Length | Transformation Rule | Required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ORDER_ID | order_identifier | VARCHAR | 20 | Hash MD5 for PII masking | Yes |
| CUST_ID | customer_key | NUMBER | 10 | Direct mapping | Yes |
| ORDER_AMT | order_amount | DECIMAL | 15,2 | Currency conversion USD→EUR | Yes |
| ORDER_DATE | order_timestamp | TIMESTAMP | - | Convert to UTC, add timezone | Yes |
| ORDER_STATUS | status_code | VARCHAR | 10 | Lookup table mapping (PENDING→P, COMPLETED→C) | Yes |
| NOTES | order_notes | VARCHAR | 500 | Null handling, trim whitespace | No |
prompt_inputs.overview_sheet:
WORKFLOW CHART:
[Oracle OLTP] → [Kafka Cluster] → [Snowflake Kafka Connector] → [Snowflake DW]
         ↓              ↓                      ↓                          ↓
    CDC Enabled    3 Topics            Auto-ingest Pipe          Materialized Views
    Change Data    (orders,            Real-time load            (aggregations)
    Capture        customers,          <5min latency
                   transactions)

WORKFLOW DESCRIPTIONS:
1. Oracle OLTP: Implements Change Data Capture (CDC) to detect INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations on source tables
2. Kafka Cluster: Receives CDC events in real-time, maintains 7-day retention, partitioned by customer_key for ordering guarantees
3. Snowflake Connector: Consumes Kafka messages, applies transformations (masking, conversions), handles schema evolution
4. Snowflake DW: Loads to staging tables, merges into fact/dimension tables, refreshes downstream materialized views for reporting

solution_criteria: Detail Design includes all four workflow components (source CDC, streaming platform, ingestion connector, target warehouse) with real-time streaming architecture
Mapping sheet covers all transformation rules for transitioning from batch to streaming, including latency-relevant operations
Design addresses the <5 minute latency requirement with specific technical choices (Kafka partitioning, auto-ingest pipes, connector configuration)

scenario: Testing with a real-time streaming ETL design transitioning from batch processing with latency requirements

Base Design Document - Customer Data Migration Project

History Updated: v2.1 - Added PII masking requirements
Overview: Migrate customer records from legacy Oracle DB to cloud PostgreSQL with encryption and masking of sensitive fields (SSN, email, phone, credit card)
Sender Spec: Oracle 11g database, 2.5M customer records, unencrypted PII fields
Receiver Spec: AWS RDS PostgreSQL, encrypted at-rest, masked PII in non-production environments
Mapping: Source columns to target columns with transformation rules
prompt_inputs.mapping_sheet:
| Physical Column | Logical Column | Data Type | Length | Rule Transfer | Required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUST_ID | CustomerID | INT | 10 | Direct copy, primary key | Yes |
| CUST_SSN | SSN | VARCHAR | 11 | Encrypt with AES-256, mask last 5 digits in non-prod | Yes |
| CUST_EMAIL | Email | VARCHAR | 100 | Encrypt with AES-256, hash for matching | Yes |
| CUST_PHONE | PhoneNumber | VARCHAR | 15 | Encrypt with AES-256, mask first 6 digits | Yes |
| CUST_CC | CreditCard | VARCHAR | 16 | Encrypt with AES-256, tokenize, never log | Yes |
| CUST_NAME | FullName | VARCHAR | 100 | Direct copy | No |
| CUST_ADDR | Address | VARCHAR | 255 | Direct copy | No |
prompt_inputs.overview_sheet:
WORKFLOW CHART:

[Oracle Source] → [Extract] → [Validate PII] → [Encrypt/Mask] → [Load] → [PostgreSQL Target]

WORKFLOW DESCRIPTIONS:
1. Extract: Read customer records from Oracle, identify PII columns
2. Validate PII: Verify data format (SSN pattern, email format, phone digits) before transformation
3. Encrypt/Mask: Apply AES-256 encryption to sensitive fields; mask PII in non-production copies; tokenize credit cards
4. Load: Insert encrypted/masked data into PostgreSQL with audit logging of all transformations
5. Verify: Validate row counts, checksum encrypted values, confirm PII is not in logs
